subject: Civil Engineering
title: Base Isolation: Floating on Bearings
description: A 60-second lesson on Base Isolation: Floating on Bearings.

hook.text: What if the building didn't feel the earthquake at all? Base isolation makes that possible.

buildup.text: Rubber bearings between the foundation and the building let the ground move underneath.

discovery.text: Lead-rubber bearings flex slowly during quakes — absorbing energy while centering the building.

twist.text: The building barely sways while the ground beneath moves inches — occupants feel almost nothing.

climax.text: Japan's base-isolated hospitals continued operating during the 2011 earthquake — fully functional.

punchline.text: Disconnect the building from the ground and the earthquake passes beneath it.

quiz.question: How do base isolation bearings protect a building?
options: They strengthen the foundation to resist earthquake forces directly
They allow the ground to move beneath the building while the structure stays relatively still
They absorb sound waves from the earthquake to reduce shaking

details.summary: Base isolation decouples a building from ground shaking by placing flexible bearings between the foundation and the superstructure. These bearings, typically lead-rubber or friction pendulum devices, allow the ground to move beneath the building while the building itself moves much less.
details.whyItMatters: Base isolation is the most effective seismic protection technology available, allowing critical facilities like hospitals to remain fully operational during major earthquakes.
takeaways: Flexible bearings between foundation and building filter out earthquake shaking
Forces on the isolated structure are reduced by 50 to 80% versus fixed-base
Hospitals, data centers, and museums are prime candidates for isolation

faq.question: How does base isolation reduce earthquake forces on a building?
faq.answer: Isolation bearings lengthen the building's natural period well beyond the range of damaging earthquake energy, typically from 0.5 seconds to 2.5 or more seconds. At these longer periods, spectral acceleration is much lower.

faq.question: What are the limitations of base isolation for earthquake protection?
faq.answer: Base isolation is expensive and requires a flexible gap around the building perimeter for bearing displacement. It is most effective for stiff, low to mid-rise buildings and less beneficial for tall, already-flexible structures.
